claims.text: The starting as-solidified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar eutectic microstructure.
The starting alloy's strength and plasticity are below industrial fastener requirements.
A post-solidification solution-and-aging heat treatment is the proposed intervention.
Solution treatment at approximately 1100°C for a short time will homogenize the microstructure and minimize segregation.
Rapid quenching followed by aging at approximately 500°C for 6–12 hours will produce fine, controlled precipitates along lamellar interfaces.
Fine interfacial precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Fine interfacial precipitates will impede grain- or phase-boundary sliding.
Secondary phases at lamellar interfaces will enhance load sharing between phases.
The precipitation-refined microstructure will resist coarsening during temperature fluctuations.
The heat-treated microstructure will reduce pathways for corrosion.
Strengthening grain or phase boundaries will retard creep.
The treatment will increase yield strength relative to the as-solidified alloy.
The treatment will increase tensile ductility relative to the as-solidified alloy.
The treatment will improve creep resistance relative to the as-solidified alloy.
The treatment will improve corrosion performance relative to the as-solidified alloy.
Key mechanical properties are expected to improve by approximately 10–20%.
The treated alloy is expected to remain relevant under temperature fluctuations from sub-zero temperatures to approximately 500°C.
The treated alloy is expected to be relevant under continuous loading, room-temperature creep, and aggressive salt-spray conditions.
